text:
The Jets' season will be told through Connor Hellebuyck for a while, whether they like it or not. The three-time Vezina winner and 2025 Hart Trophy winner asked for a trade, was suspended for not reporting to camp, and was sent to New Jersey on Oct. 23 for a package led by Dawson Mercer. He comes back to Winnipeg with the Devils on Tuesday, though New Jersey says he won't start. Stuart Skinner, signed to a two-year deal last week, is the man in that crease now.

The team in front of him has finally started winning. Three straight, 15-9, and the chances back it: 63% of the expected goals in those games, including a comeback against Montreal that the headlines called historic and Sunday's last-second win over Tampa Bay. Over the season the picture is weaker: 7-8-3, 47.6% of the expected goals, and about seven fewer goals than the chances usually produce.

The top line of Mark Scheifele, Kyle Connor and Cole Perfetti is doing its job (9-6 in goals, 52% of the chances). Neal Pionk and Dylan Samberg are steady. Depth scoring is thin, and that is where Mercer has to matter. Our simulations put Winnipeg at 18% to make the playoffs, projecting about 83 points, which means this hot week has to become a hot month. Tuesday is loud. What follows it decides more.
